text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for Helion Dynamics (customer: helion-dyn, tenant: hd-prod-7) in eu1-dedicated-pool-03. p99 > 4.2s for 14m — SLO breach. Pager: @oncall_kevin. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/helion-latency

oncall_kevin: I'm on it, paging SRE runbook. Starting triage.

alice_sre: +1 joining. Can someone post recent tail of /metrics and tail of inference logs for tenant hd-prod-7?

miguel_runtime: grabbing metrics — CPU & GPU look fine, but KV cache miss rate for this tenant jumped from 18% -> 86%. Also seeing many long tail requests with big seq_len (avg 1.2k).

samira_account: Helion is reporting user-facing slowdowns for a subset of clients on EU region. They're on a low-latency SLA. I'm on the call with their Eng (on standby).

alice_sre: OK, hypothesis: tenant noise (large context inputs) is starving CPU/GPU scheduling causing head-of-line latency. Two fast mitigations: 1) isolate tenant to own pool or 2) apply tenant-level rate limiting / sampling. Which is faster?

miguel_runtime: We can do tenant isolation (evict to spare pool) but need to confirm spare capacity in eu1. Running `rbac list-pools --region eu1 --free` now.

ops-bot: Spare capacity in eu1: free-gpu-pods=2 (each can host ~250 rps depending on model). Warm spare flag: true.

oncall_kevin: If spare exists, do isolation. Samira, notify customer this may cause brief reconnects.

samira_account: telling Helion: "We're initiating a targeted mitigation (tenant isolation) to restore SLOs; brief switch expected (~30-90s). We'll update in <5m>." They ack.

jordan_support: What about fallback model? Could we route Helion to a smaller quantized variant while we isolate? Less ideal for quality but buys time.

miguel_runtime: We have rdm-quant-8bit available in eu1. Routing policy change takes ~15s to flip. Two-step plan: 1) route new requests to rdm-quant-8bit, 2) evict tenant to spare pool and restore cache.

alice_sre: I'll run eviction. Command I will execute (tracked):
```bash
# isolate tenant hd-prod-7 to spare pool
redwoodctl tenant evict --tenant hd-prod-7 --from-pool dedicated-pool-03 --to-pool spare-dedicated-01 --dry-run=false
```

oncall_kevin: Proceed. I'll be primary comms for external updates. Alice, tag me on status updates every 30s.

alice_sre: Executing now.

ops-bot: Action accepted: eviction job 0x8b3 started. Estimated completion 45s.

miguel_runtime: Flipping routing to rdm-quant-8bit now to reduce CPU time for inflight and new requests.

ops-bot: Routing change complete. New requests are hitting rdm-quant-8bit (eu1).

samira_account: Helion: "Routing to fallback model now; visible latency should improve, quality change limited to some long-form completions." They say they're comfortable with that for 10-15m.

alice_sre: Eviction completed. Verifying KV cache warm-up on spare-dedicated-01. Starting prefix cache priming for hd-prod-7.

miguel_runtime: Cache priming showing progress — miss rate dropping -> 20% within 2m. p95/p99 trending down. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/helion-hd-prod-7

oncall_kevin: Good. Samira, let Helion know we're seeing p99 back under SLO (3s) on fallback. Plan next: monitor for 10m, then either keep routing or rollback to original model when cache is warm.

samira_account: Sent update to Helion and scheduled a post-incident call. They asked for timeline for full rollback — we'll confirm after monitoring window.

leyla_pm: Noted for incident summary: customer impact (subset of EU users), mitigation steps (fallback model + tenant isolation to spare pool), duration so far ~12m. Please add exact metric deltas to the postmortem.

alice_sre: Adding markers to timeline and saving logs. Log stash: `s3://redwood-incidents/1768001111/`

miguel_runtime: Taking a look at why tenant sent large seq_len requests — looks like a batch job from Helion analytics ramped around the same time. Recommend we add tenant-level admission controls for seq_len and a protective policy for dedicated pools.

oncall_kevin: Agreed. Immediate next steps: 1) monitor 10m, 2) keep Helion on fallback if p99 stable, 3) open follow-up action to add admission control & tenant shielding. I'll handoff to alice_sre for detailed mitigation notes.

alice_sre: I'm taking runbook lead. Handoff: oncall_kevin -> alice_sre at 1768002100.

oncall_kevin: Thanks team. I'm clear to return to rotation for now. Leaving incident to Alice + Miguel.

ops-bot: Reminder: create incident-# ticket and assign to eng-runtime + accounts for RCA. `incident create --severity P1 --customer helion-dyn --assignees miguel_runtime,samira_account`

alice_sre: Created incident ticket IR-1768001111 and scheduled postmortem meeting. Will include recommended mitigations: tenant admission caps, warm-spare sizing, and runbook updates.

samira_account: Helion requested export of logs and timeline once we have the postmortem. I'll coordinate.

miguel_runtime: Monitoring window looks stable at +8m: p99 back to 1.5s, p95 ~ 220ms. Leaving fallback in place for now; will test rollback when cache stable and no batch activity detected.

alice_sre: Closing warboard for now. If anything spikes again, reopen thread. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:
